editorial.overview: The Praxis Physics: Content Knowledge (5265) exam measures the knowledge and skills required for beginning secondary school physics teachers. Certified by ETS, this assessment covers six distinct domains, including mechanics, electricity, and modern physics. It evaluates conceptual understanding, analytical thinking, and problem-solving abilities through 125 selected-response questions, ensuring candidates possess the necessary subject matter expertise for classroom instruction.
editorial.preparation_strategy: Review the test specifications to understand the 125 questions. Create a personalized study plan based on the six content domains. Practice with sample questions to become familiar with the computer-delivered format. Since calculators are prohibited, focus on conceptual understanding and problem-solving techniques. Use the provided tables of physical constants and conversion factors to guide your review of physics principles.
editorial.who_should_take: This exam is for individuals pursuing a teaching career in secondary school physics. Candidates have typically completed or nearly completed a bachelor’s degree program with appropriate coursework in physics and education to demonstrate their readiness for the classroom.
